{ "source": "{% extends 'OT Layout' %} {% block content %} {% comment %} Access denied (PP-01, PP-16). The wording is deliberately identical whether the record exists, does not exist, or exists and is not yours. Saying "this case is not assigned to you" would confirm the case exists, which is disclosure by another route. No technical detail is shown. The correlation id is rendered only so a user can quote it to support; the underlying error is logged separately. It DOES show the reader their own identity and their own web roles, and that is not a disclosure: it is the one fact they cannot look up for themselves and the only one that explains this page. "I hold the AQS reviewer role and still cannot see the AQS page" is unanswerable from the outside — the role could be attached to a different contact, the sign-in could have resolved to a contact nobody granted anything to, or the session could be holding roles from before a grant. Every one of those looks identical from the reader's chair, and every one of them is settled by printing what the portal actually resolved for them. PP-16 is about not confirming whether a RECORD exists. A person's own roles are neither a record they are being denied nor anyone else's business. {% endcomment %}

You do not have access to this page

This may be because the page is restricted to a different role, or because the record is not one you work on. If you think you should have access, contact your Outcome Testing manager.

{% if user %} You are signed in as {{ user.fullname | escape }} {% if user.emailaddress1 %}({{ user.emailaddress1 | escape }}){% endif %}. {% else %} You are not signed in. Sign in and try again. {% endif %}

{% if user %} {% comment %} What the portal resolved, not what anyone believes was granted. `user.roles` is the same list the access rules are evaluated against, so if a role a person was given is missing here, it was never reaching the rules and no amount of checking the rules would have found that. A stale session is the common cause and the cheapest thing to rule out, which is why signing out is offered first rather than as a last resort. {% endcomment %}

Your roles on this site: {% assign role_count = 0 %} {% for role in user.roles %}{% assign role_count = role_count | plus: 1 %}{% endfor %} {% if role_count > 0 %} {% for role in user.roles %}{{ role | escape }}{% unless forloop.last %}, {% endunless %}{% endfor %}. {% else %} none. Nothing on this site is open to an account with no role, which is why this page is where you landed. {% endif %}

If a role you were granted is not in that list, the portal has not picked it up for this session yet. Sign out and sign back in, and if it is still missing, send this page's contents to your Outcome Testing manager — it says which account the site is treating you as, which is the part nobody can check from the other side.
